decision.rule: target n = max(150 L1 floor, n_required); >= 40 L5 (D-010; FR-002) -- the floor is never lowered
decision.n_required_basis: conservative detectable-effect figure for the observed effect (+0.1123 at 95%, sigma_d = max over the five committed CI rows); the decision is framing-invariant -- even the 80%-power figure (109) stays under the 150 floor
decision.statement: Target DS-v2 = 150 L1 queries (max(150, 54) = 150; all four kinds -- callers/definition/flow/impact -- represented) plus >= 40 L5. At 150 evaluated queries the minimum certifiable two-sided-95% effect is ~+0.061 (matched sigma) to +0.067 (conservative sigma): the observed +0.1123 certifies with ~1.7x margin; a half-effect +0.05 would need 220-269 evaluated queries at CI-clearing (450-549 at 80% power), beyond the authoring budget -- recorded as out of reach, not silently dropped.

method.name: Sakai-style topic-set-size design; two-sided paired test at alpha=0.05; detectable-effect framing (primary) with an 80%-power paired variant (secondary)
method.approximation: closed-form normal approximation (Sakai's paired-t Excel tools implement the same detectable-effect logic via the noncentral t); formulas stated so every figure is recomputable with stdlib arithmetic
method.evaluated_n_mapping: DS-v1's evidence unit is its 29-query validate split (seeded 50/50 of 58 L1, D-006). DS-v2's accept gate bootstraps pooled per-query paired differences with each query validate-side exactly once across the seeded >=5-fold rotation (D-009: 'a legitimate n=all-queries test'), so required n in evaluated queries maps 1:1 onto the L1 authoring total -- this makes max(150, n_required) a like-for-like comparison. Under DS-v1's fixed-split convention the mapping would be 2:1; DS-v2 does not use that convention for its accept gate.
references: Sakai, 'Topic Set Size Design', Information Retrieval Journal 2016 (https://dl.acm.org/doi/10.1145/2911451.2911492)
Smucker, Allan & Carterette, CIKM'07 (paired bootstrap is a first-class test)
Urbano et al., arXiv:1905.11096 (small query sets systematically under-detect true effects)

inputs.n_validate_source: benchmarks/quality/ablation.json dataset.split.validate (seeded 50/50 split of the 58 L1 queries, D-006)
inputs.bootstrap_protocol: paired bootstrap vs the incumbent's validate recall 0.2521, 10,000 resamples, 95% CI (benchmarks/quality/ablation.md Figure 2)
inputs.per_query_matrices: not present in the committed record (the /tmp sweep artifacts named in ablation.json measurement.provenance are session-local and absent on this machine); sigma_d is derived from the committed 95% CI half-widths at n=29 -- the derivation input is itself committed evidence
inputs.constraints: arithmetic over committed evidence only; no retrieval sweeps, no model inference, nothing re-measured

derived.half_width_range_note: reproduces the ablation record's 'widths ~ +/-0.13-0.15' statement at n=29

sigma_matched.rationale: the best near-miss's own CI -- the candidate DS-v2's first re-test is expected to carry

derived.sigma_conservative_rationale: max over the five committed CI rows; guards against an unknown future candidate having the largest observed dispersion

a_observed_effect.note: all four framings <= 150, so the D-010 floor governs and certifies the observed effect with margin

b_half_effect.note: beyond the D-010 authoring budget (and the ~3-5x envelope); recorded as out of reach -- at 150, effects smaller than ~+0.06 remain undetectable at 95%

cross_checks.sqrt_n_direct_route: ceil(29 * (0.1377/0.1123)^2) = 44 = n_detectable_matched -- shrinking the best candidate's own half-width agrees with the sigma_d route (algebraically identical, numerically equal)
cross_checks.rq4_arithmetic: h(120) = 0.1377 * sqrt(29/120) = 0.067693 ~= the '~+/-0.07-0.08 at n~120' of specs/retrieval-quality-v2/research.md RQ4 (re-derived from the committed CI, not copied)
cross_checks.ds1_failure_quantified: at n=29, delta_min = z * sigma_matched / sqrt(29) = 0.1377 = exactly the measured half-width -- Urbano et al.'s small-set under-detection regime, the expected behavior rather than an anomaly
